what_it_measured.text: Improvements in QoL during afamelanotide treatment were measured using two QoL tools, with good correlation observed between these two instruments.
Changes in the time to phototoxic symptom onset, QoL, and laboratory parameters were assessed before and during treatment with afamelanotide.

dose.text: Afamelanotide (16 mg) was administered subcutaneously as frequently as every 8 weeks, with a maximum of 6 implants per year.

route.text: Afamelanotide (16 mg) was administered subcutaneously as frequently as every 8 weeks, with a maximum of 6 implants per year.

endpoint.text: Improvements in QoL during afamelanotide treatment were measured using two QoL tools, with good correlation observed between these two instruments.
Changes in the time to phototoxic symptom onset, QoL, and laboratory parameters were assessed before and during treatment with afamelanotide.
The outcomes included changes in time until phototoxic symptoms, QoL, and laboratory parameters before versus during afamelanotide treatment.

reported_results.text: Among the patients who received ≥2 implants, the median time to symptom onset following sunlight exposure was 12.5 min (IQR, 5–20) prior to the initiation of afamelanotide and 120 min (IQR, 60–240) after treatment (p < 0.001).
Results: A total of 29 patients with protoporphyria were included, 26 of whom (72.2%) received ≥2 afamelanotide implants.
Moreover, 100% of patients who received ≥2 doses of afamelanotide reported a decrease in the frequency and Life 2024, 14, x FOR PEER REVIEW 4 of 9 severity of their phototoxic reactions.

Among the 26 patients who received at least 2 implants, the median time to symptom onset following sunlight exposure was 12.5 min (IQR, 5–20) prior to initiation of afamelanotide and 120 min (IQR, 60–240) after treatment (p < 0.0001, Figure 1A).

The median EPP-QoL score prior to afamelanotide initiation was 27.8 (IQR, 18.1–51.4), improving to 75 (IQR, 63.2–86.1) during treatment (p = 0.00067, Figure 1B), with thesechanges sustained over time (Figure 2A).
The median metal-free erythrocyte 6protoporphyrin levels increased from 1185 µg/dL (IQR, 815–1722) before treatment to 1419 µg/dL (IQR, 801–1908) during treatment (p = 0.014, Figure 3A).
